name: Julia Thiele-Schuerhoff
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Julia Thiele-Schuerhoff inherited a portion of the fortune that her late father, Heinz Hermann Thiele, built up, including a stake in vehicle braking systems maker Knorr-Bremse AG.
Her father joined Knorr-Bremse's legal department in the late 1960s and took over control in the mid-1980s.
He withdrew from operational duties in 2007, chaired the supervisory board, was named honorary chairman in 2016, and took the company public in 2018.
When he died in February 2021, at age 79, Heinz Hermann also owned 50% of railroad equipment maker Vossloh and 12.4% of German airline Lufthansa.
Julia Thiele-Schuerhoff serves on Knorr-Bremse's supervisory board and runs an affiliated charity organization, Knorr-Bremse Global Care.
forbes_facts: She is cofounder of Knorr-Bremse Global Care, established in 2005 following the devastating tsunami in Southeast Asia.
Operating worldwide, it supports projects run by partner organizations in education, emergency relief and water, sanitation and hygiene.

name: Jacques D'Amours
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Jacques D'Amours cofounded Canadian convenience store conglomerate Alimentation Couche-Tard in 1980.
He retired as VP of administration in 2014 and retired from the company's board in 2023.
Couche-Tard has ballooned by snatching up competitors, including Minnesota-based Holiday Stationstores for $1.6 billion in 2017.
The company now boasts annual sales of $73 billion and more than 17,000 owned or franchised stores worldwide.

name: Anthony Langley
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Tony Langley owns Nottinghamshire, UK-based engineering and manufacturing giant Langley Holdings.
Langley started the business in 1975, at age 20, with what was left of his grandfather's failed engineering firm.
He launched Langley Mining, which sold equipment to the UK coal industry and eventually moved to steel, oil and gas customers as well.
He has diversified through acquisitions, including buying crane manufacturer Clarke Chapman from Rolls-Royce in 2000 and Bergen Engines (also from Rolls-Royce) in 2021.
Langley is now pivoting the group to provide behind-the-meter power solutions for the AI data center boom.
Langley Holdings employs 5,500 people across more than 90 subsidiaries and generates annual revenues of around $2 billion.
forbes_facts: An accomplished yachtsman, Langley owns the Gladiator Sailing Team that competes in elite racing competition.
In 2016, Langley agreed to house 80 Syrian refugees in surplus office space in Germany after a request from the local government.

name: Stephen Lansdown
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Stephen Lansdown cofounded Hargreaves Lansdown, a British financial services firm.
The company manages over $100 billion in assets and boasts more than 1.7 million clients.
Lansdown stepped down as chairman of the firm in 2009 and left its board in 2012.
In 2010 he relocated to Guernsey, where he was a non-executive director of Ravenscroft Group, an investment services firm based on the island. He retired as chairman in 2021.
Lansdown cofounded Earth Capital, a private equity firm focused on sustainable and impact investing, in 2008. It shut down in 2024.
forbes_facts: Lansdown owns Bristol Sport, which oversees the commercial operations of Bristol City F.C., Bristol Rugby Club, Bristol City W.F.C., Bristol Flyers and DZ Racing.

name: Susan Williams
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Hurun Global (2020-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Susan Slavik Williams owns about 5% of industrial supply firm W.W. Grainger, which did $10.8 billion in net sales in 2017.
Since 1989, Williams has served as a director of Mark IV Capital, a real estate firm based in Newport Beach, California.
She sits on the board of the St. Louis Zoo and on the Friends Committee of Missouri Baptist Hospital.
Williams serves as CEO of the Donald Slavik Family Foundation, which focuses on protecting wildlife and educating the public on environmental issues.
forbes_facts: Williams and her husband Felix owned a custom home electronics firm called the Screening Room for 10 years.

name: Katarina Martinson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Katarina Martinson and her sister Louise Lindh each own a 15% stake in their family's investment outfit L.E. Lundbergforetagen AB.
The company holds interests in property management and a variety of other investments, including a pulp and paper company.
Both sisters have board seats in the group companies along with their father Fredrik Lundberg.
The company was founded by their paternal grandfather Lars in 1944 as a construction outfit. Fredrik took over management of the firm in 1981.
Privately Martinson is an active investor and owns stakes in clothing company NN07 and online cosmetics seller Lyko.
forbes_facts: Martinson reportedly spent roughly $15 million in 2017 on a townhouse in central Stockholm, one of the most expensive house ever sold in Sweden.
She chairs industrial group Indutrade -- which L.E. Lundbergforetagen invests in -- making her the youngest chairman of a company on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.

name: Sjamsul Nursalim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2024)
forbes_bio: The son of a rubber seller, Sjamsul Nursalim made his fortune in tire, property, coal and retail businesses.
His Singapore-headquartered Giti Tire is a global player, selling to more than 130 countries.
He owns a stake in listed retailer Mitra Adiperkasa, which operates Zara, Topshop, Steve Madden and other retail brands in Indonesia.
His family also owns a stake in Singapore-listed Tuan Sing Holdings, which develops and owns a range of properties.
forbes_facts: Giti jointly developed the tires used in BYD's hypercar Yangwang U9 Xtreme, which set a new world speed record for mass-produced cars in September 2025.

name: Zhao Weiguo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022-2023); Forbes annual (2017-2022); Hurun Global (2017-2022); Hurun China (2016-2021)
forbes_bio: Zhao Weiguo leads Tsinghua Unigroup, an affiliate of Tsinghua University, and has been a force in building up the country's semiconductor industry.
Zhao is a Tsinghua University alum.

name: Alexey Repik
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2020)
forbes_bio: Alexey Repik is founder of R-Pharm, one of Russia's largest pharmaceutical companies and one of the biggest state contractors.
In 2017 Mitsui & Co., Ltd. acquired 10% shares of R-Pharm for $200 million.
Repik started R-Pharm in 2001 with $40,000 in startup capital, half of which came from his mother.
Repik got his first job in healthcare in 1995.
forbes_facts: Repik is president of the Russian Business Association 'Delovaya Rossiya' ('Business Russia'), which unites more than 7,000 entrepreneurs.
He is donating for construction of a large shelter for 1,500 dogs per year in Yaroslavl, a city 250 kilometers from Moscow.

name: Leng Youbin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2009-2026)
forbes_bio: Leng Youbin is the chairman and CEO of China Feihe, one of the country's largest suppliers of infant formula.
Leng, who herded cows as a child, worked at a state-owned dairy farm for about a decade before striking out on his own.
The mogul acquired stakes in the farm and a dairy plant, and started to sell milk and infant formula under the Feihe brand.
The company went public in Hong Kong in 2019, and today owns 11 plants and 12 farms with 100,000 cows and goats.
forbes_facts: Leng graduated from Northeast Agricultural University in China's northeast Heilongjiang Province in 1995 through a correspondence course.
He holds an executive MBA degree from Peking University.

name: Constantinos Martinos
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Constantinos Martinos is the owner of Greek shipping firm Thenamaris, which has a fleet of 87 tankers, bulk carriers, container ships and LNG carriers.
He cofounded the company in 1972 with his mother and two brothers. His brothers, Athanasios and Andreas, split off in 1990 and 1998, respectively, leaving him with Thenamaris.
Collectively, Constantinos and his brothers own the largest shipping fleet in Greece, the largest shipowning nation in the world.
Thenamaris is now run by his son, Nikolas. His other son Ioannis runs shipping services firm Signal Group.

name: Nicholas Pritzker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Nicholas (Nick) Pritzker is a cousin of the late Jay Pritzker and his brothers Donald and Robert, who built the Hyatt hotel chain.
Pritzker spent many years leading Hyatt's hotel development efforts, but he has since sold most of his Hyatt stock.
He has shifted his attention and investment dollars to causes like clean energy, marijuana legalization and criminal justice reform.
He is cofounder and chairman emeritus of Evergreen Climate Innovations, which invests in clean energy companies in the Midwest.
Pritzker invested early in the e-cigarette maker Juul, Uber and Tesla through his investment firm, Tao Capital.
forbes_facts: In the 2016 election, Pritzker donated to Proposition 64, a ballot initiative in California which successfully legalized marijuana in the Golden State.
